'''Michael Häupl''' (born 14 September 1949) is an [[Austria|Austrian]] politician. A member of the [[SPÖ|Social Democratic Party of Austria]] (SPÖ), he served as [[List of mayors of Vienna|mayor and governor]] of [[Vienna]] from 1994 to 2018.

==Early life and education==
Häupl was born in [[Altlengbach]], a small town in [[Lower Austria]]. He studied biology and zoology at the [[University of Vienna]]. He subsequently worked in the herpetological collection of the [[Natural History Museum, Vienna|Natural History Museum Vienna]] from 1975 to 1983.<ref name="parlamentgv">{{cite web|title=Biografie von Dr. Michael Häupl|url=https://www.parlament.gv.at/WWER/PAD_02884/|website=Österreichisches Parlament}}</ref>

==Political career==
Häupl led the [[Socialist Students of Austria]] from 1975 to 1977. From 1983 to 1988, he served as a member of the [[Municipal Council and Landtag of Vienna]], and subsequently as City Councillor for Sport and the Environment. He became leader of the Vienna branch of the SPÖ in 1993, and succeeded [[Helmut Zilk]] as Mayor and Governor of Vienna on 7 November 1994.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Michael Häupl |url=https://www.geschichtewiki.wien.gv.at/Michael_H%C3%A4upl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251014081939/https://www.geschichtewiki.wien.gv.at/Michael_H%C3%A4upl |archive-date=2025-10-14 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=www.geschichtewiki.wien.gv.at |language=de}}</ref>

In the 1996 state election, the SPÖ lost its absolute majority in the Vienna State Parliament for the first time, receiving 39.15 per cent of the vote and 43 of the 100 seats. It subsequently formed a coalition government with the [[Austrian People's Party]] (ÖVP). The SPÖ regained its absolute majority in the 2001 election and retained it in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-25 |title=Wahl-Rückblick: Die Dominanz der SPÖ in Wien im Verlauf der Jahrzehnte |url=https://www.meinbezirk.at/wien/c-politik/die-dominanz-der-spoe-in-wien-im-verlauf-der-jahrzehnte_a7120410 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=MeinBezirk.at |language=de}}</ref> Following the [[2010 Viennese state election|2010 election]], in which the SPÖ fell one seat short of an absolute majority, Häupl formed a coalition with the [[The Greens (Austria)|Greens]], creating Austria's first red–green state government. This coalition remained in office for two terms.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-28 |title=Grüne, Neos & ÖVP: Das waren die vergangenen Koalitionen der SPÖ in Wien |url=https://www.meinbezirk.at/wien/c-politik/das-waren-die-vergangenen-koalitionen-der-spoe-in-wien_a7130187 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=MeinBezirk.at |language=de}}</ref> Häupl stepped down as mayor in 2018, midway through his fifth term, after 23 years in office, and was succeeded by [[Michael Ludwig]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-05-25 |title=Ludwig mit deutlicher Mehrheit gewählt: Bürgermeister mit 56 von... |url=https://www.diepresse.com/5434758/ludwig-mit-deutlicher-mehrheit-gewaehlt-buergermeister-mit-56-von-99-gueltigen-stimmen |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=Die Presse |language=de}}</ref>

During his tenure as mayor, Häupl oversaw the development of several new urban districts, including [[Seestadt Aspern]], the Sonnwendviertel and the Nordbahnviertel, as well as the expansion of the [[Vienna U-Bahn]] network, which grew from 57 stations at the beginning of his mayoralty to 98 stations by the time he left office.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Häupl had a daughter from his first marriage. His second marriage was to Helga Häupl-Seitz, with whom he had a son. On May 20, 2011, he married Barbara Hörnlein, who in 2015 became medical director of the Otto Wagner Hospital, and until around June 2016, medical director of the Wilhelminenspital, after which she became director of the Vienna Regional Health Insurance Fund.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Häupl-Ehefrau wird WGKK-Chefin |url=http://m.kurier.at/chronik/wien/haeupl-ehefrau-wird-wgkk-chefin/205.911.573 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624080958/http://m.kurier.at/chronik/wien/haeupl-ehefrau-wird-wgkk-chefin/205.911.573 |archive-date=2016-06-24 |access-date=2026-07-25 |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Baltaci |first=von Köksal |date=2015-08-05 |title=Asklepios-Obmann: "Ich sollte mundtot gemacht werden" |url=https://www.diepresse.com/4776773/asklepios-obmann-ich-sollte-mundtot-gemacht-werden |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=Die Presse |language=de}}</ref>

In his younger years, Renate Brauner, a city councillor and former deputy mayor until 2018, was his partner. Their close friendship has endured to this day; as Die Presse wrote in October 2010, "Häupl can rely on few people as blindly as he does on his deputy."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwaiger |first=von Rosemarie |date=2016-09-03 |title=Wiener SPÖ: Eine schrecklich nette Familie |url=https://www.diepresse.com/600908/wiener-spoe-eine-schrecklich-nette-familie |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=Die Presse |language=de}}</ref>

In 2024, Häupl revealed that he had been diagnosed with [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=red |first=wien ORF at |date=December 14, 2024 |title=Michael Häupl an Parkinson erkrankt |url=https://wien.orf.at/stories/3285336/ |access-date=February 6, 2026 |website=wien.ORF.at |language=de}}</ref>
